claims.text: The initial material is an equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr random solid solution.
The random HfNbTaTiZr state has significant local lattice distortion.
The random state has a broadened high-frequency phonon DOS.
Annealing or Monte Carlo evolution induces chemical short-range ordering in HfNbTaTiZr.
The induced SRO consists specifically of HfTi and TiZr B2-like ordered binary clusters.
The B2-like clusters can nucleate and percolate while the alloy retains an overall single-phase BCC structure.
A temperature range of 800–1200 K is sufficient for SRO evolution while remaining below the solvus for distinct phase separation.
Ordering reduces the variance of atomic bond lengths and angles within the B2-like domains.
Reduced bond-length and bond-angle variance gives the ordered domains lower phonon-scattering cross-sections than the random matrix.
The lower scattering cross-sections narrow high-frequency phonon linewidths.
The transition from a random state to B2-like ordering reduces fluctuations in the local potential-energy landscape.
B2-like ordering reduces the RMS atomic displacement amplitude.
Reduced RMS displacement enhances the group velocity of high-frequency optical and acoustic phonons.
Reduced RMS displacement increases the lifetimes of high-frequency optical and acoustic phonons.
Percolation of ordered clusters provides continuous low-scattering pathways for phonon transport.
The reduction in disorder scattering outweighs scattering from the remaining disordered regions and increases lattice thermal conductivity relative to the random state.
The conductivity increase is accompanied by sharper high-frequency phonon-DOS peaks.
The conductivity increase is accompanied by lower Debye-Waller factors for elements participating in the ordered clusters.
The conductivity-increase regime begins only when the ordered clusters exceed a percolation threshold.
Distinct precipitate formation or sufficiently large chemical and interfacial mismatch can reverse the benefit and make interface scattering dominant.
